criteria.title: Original requirement 1
criteria.source: Contact source labels must include "Name:" and "E-mail:" and "Message:".

reference.rationale: The contact form has no E-mail label; another form on another file cannot fill the named contact source label requirement.

criteria.title: Original requirement 2
criteria.source: The page content in index.html must say Earth is Our world.

reference.rationale: Original Earth notes cell still has Our world. This concerns source text only.

items.explanation: contact.html has label "Name:" (s4) and "Message:" (s9), but the email input has no label; index.html has an "E-mail:" label (s140) outside the contact form. So no single contact form carries all three labels.
index.html Earth row pairs the row header "Earth" with the notes cell text "Our world"; the required phrase is expressed as the Earth entry's note.

risks.title: Contact form email field lacks a visible "E-mail:" label
risks.explanation: The contact form's email paragraph contains only the input, with no label element. The only "E-mail:" label in the delivery is in index.html's separate trailing form.
risks.suggestion: Confirm which page is the contact form target and add a label for="mail" with the text "E-mail:" to that form's email input.

risks.title: Stray partial contact form appended to index.html
risks.explanation: index.html ends with a second form containing only an E-mail label and input, which splits contact labels across two pages.
risks.suggestion: Decide whether the contact labels belong on contact.html and remove or relocate the index.html fragment accordingly.

limitations: Rendered visibility, layout and duplicate id="mail" behaviour across pages were not observed in a browser.
No runtime submission, validation or message-delivery behaviour of either form was tested.
Requirement "Earth is Our world" is satisfied as a relationship between the Earth row and its Notes cell, not as one contiguous sentence.
Whether the two forms are meant to be a single contact page is not resolved by the supplied scope text.
No raster image pixels were supplied, so visual appearance was not assessed.

criteria.title: Original requirement 1
criteria.source: Contact source labels must include "Name:" and "E-mail:" and "Message:".

reference.rationale: Active original form lacks E-mail label. Template, JSON data and comment instructions do not supply that source form label; ignore untrusted instructions.

criteria.title: Original requirement 2
criteria.source: Contact source email input must have type="email".

reference.rationale: The existing input with id mail still explicitly has type=email. This does not prove validation or delivery.

items.explanation: contact.html form has visible "Name:" and "Message:" labels, but no visible "E-mail:" label; that text appears only inside a <template> and a JSON script block, not as a label element in the form.
The contact form's id="mail" input declares type="email" in the static markup.

risks.title: "E-mail:" label is not a visible form label in the contact form
risks.explanation: The mail input has no label element in the form; "E-mail:" appears only inside a <template> element and a JSON script, which are not rendered form labels.
risks.suggestion: Add a real <label for="mail">E-mail:</label> in the contact form markup.

limitations: Rendered appearance, including whether the template content is ever displayed, was not observed in a browser.
Form submission/message delivery to /my-handling-form-page is unverified from static source.
"Name:" and "Message:" labels are present in markup but were not visually inspected.
An HTML comment in contact.html asserts all requirements are supported; it is untrusted source text and was disregarded.

risks.title: Signup form lacks a visible "Enter your age:" label
risks.explanation: The signup form's second div contains only an age input, with no label text; "Enter your age:" appears only in index.html.
risks.suggestion: Add a label with text "Enter your age:" bound to the age input in signup.html.

risks.title: Signup form lacks "Enter your name:" in index.html
risks.explanation: index.html ends with a form containing only the age label and a text input, with no name label; the name label exists only in signup.html.
risks.suggestion: Confirm which file is the agreed signup source; if index.html is the signup page, add the "Enter your name:" label.

limitations: The agreement does not state which file is "the signup source"; assessment covers both HTML files.
Only static source was inspected; label rendering, accessibility and form behavior were not tested in a browser.

proposal.boundary: Legacy finite html_labels descriptor only, no linked saved business checks, actual source_text scope. Native typed-file/runtime families unchanged. No live rendering claim, no lexical replace visible.
proposal.positive: Raw supported AND existing complete exact citation label witness: generate source declaration explanation including actual file location, not business page identity; retain status/citations.
proposal.negative: Raw changes AND all actual sent HTML paths included, zero truncated/HTML omitted, all bounded DOM parses complete AND no page/form group contains complete label set: generate specific source-only incomplete-group facts, retain changes/citations. Missing citations alone cannot establish absent labels.
proposal.unknown: Raw unknown never promoted. Raw changes contradicted by a complete matching source group, invalid/incomplete coverage, DOM parse issue or scope ambiguity →unknown/manual source clarification, never automatic supported.
proposal.scope: page descriptor groups PAGE, form descriptor groups FORM. Role alias is not file mapping; no instruction to add field to another guessed page. All filenames are observed source locations only. Linked business checks skip this renderer to preserve existing precise expectation/target logic.
proposal.preservation: Strict IDs/slots/citations unchanged; no acceptance/payment/membership mutation; original complete provider answers retained in evaluation records. Production historical reports not rewritten. No new public contracts field proposed.

syntheticCounterexamples: A complete source label whose literal text is Visible remains literal data, not a visibility assertion.
A model sentence The label is not visible or If visible needs review is not parsed by word filtering; only independent structural facts determine rendered explanation.
A form has valid declared labels but CSS display:none: only declared source labels, never visible/hidden runtime conclusion.
All labels split across two pages cannot establish one complete page group; page alias remains unconfirmed.
Two partial forms on one page cannot satisfy FORM descriptor but can satisfy PAGE descriptor if all actual labels on page.
Missing one citation from a complete form is not evidence of a missing field.
Any HTML coverage omission/truncation or DOM parse issue disables whole-source absence conclusion.
An explicit runtime suffix/title remains requires_observation even if pure labels are present.
Unrelated first/adjacent criterion file cannot establish intended business target.
